title: A question about rice, an answer about meals
odia:
ଚାଉଳ ସେରକ କେତେ
ନା’ ମୁଁ ମଠରେ ଖାଏ।
literal_meaning: “How much is a ser of rice?” “I eat at the monastery.”
meaning_odia: ଚାଉଳ ସେରକର ଦାମ ପଚାରିଲେ ଉତ୍ତର ଆସୁଛି—ମୁଁ ମଠରେ ଖାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ପଚରାଯାଇଥିବା କଥାର ଉତ୍ତର ନଦେଇ ନିଜର ଅଲଗା ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାର କଥା କହିବାର ଅମେଳ ଏଠାରେ ଧରାପଡ଼ିଛି।
explanation: The question asks for a price; the reply supplies a place of eating. That mismatch makes the exchange comic. Read editorially, it can describe someone who answers from their own arrangements while leaving the practical question unanswered.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Asked how much a commute costs, someone replies that they work from home. A listener recalls this exchange because the reply describes a personal arrangement without supplying the requested fare.
cultural_context: ସେରକ places the question in the language of measuring rice. ମଠରେ shifts the reply away from the market to a place where the speaker eats. The change of subject, rather than a specified monastic custom, carries the joke.
